30.text:
**Pattern and choice**
Condition + भने
**पानी पर्यो भने म जाँदिनँ** (if it rains, I will not go)
pānī paryo bhane, ma gharmā baschu
If it rains, I will stay home.

**पानी पर्यो भने म जाँदिनँ** (if it rains, I will not go) gives an if-condition. **यदि** can make if explicit but is optional.
 Place भने after the condition in **यदि…भने…**.
2. Past-looking form in a future condition

**भोलि पानी पर्यो भने** (if it rains tomorrow) can refer to rain tomorrow.
 The form पर्यो does not force a report that rain has already occurred; the conditional supposes the occurrence as completed.
3. छ भने (if there is; if someone is) versus भयो भने (if it happens/comes about)

**समय छ भने** (if there is time) conditions on having time; **समय भयो भने** (if time becomes available/when the time comes) can condition on time becoming available/the time arriving.
 The state/occurrence contrast survives inside a conditional.
4. नभए versus भए पनि (even if/although it is)

**समय नभए** (if there is no time) means if there is no time; **समय भए पनि** (even if there is time) even if there is time.
 Prefix न negates the condition; -**ए पनि** (even if/although, part of a linking pattern) makes it concessive.

**जब आउनुहुन्छ** (when you/he/she comes, respectful)**, तब…** links the time of arrival; **आउनुभयो भने** (if you/he/she comes, respectful)… conditions on an arrival.
 The speech verb भन्नु in **भन्नुभयो** has a separate role from conditional भने.
Practice focus: भए introduces a condition (“if there is”). भएपछि means after that happens; भएर links a cause/circumstance.
भने can mark the condition even without यदि.

31.text:
**Pattern and choice**
Opinions with मलाई लाग्छ (I think/it seems to me that…)
**मलाई लाग्छ** (I think/it seems to me that…)…
① Start with one example
**भोलि पानी पर्छ जस्तो लाग्छ।**
bholi pānī parcha jasto lāgcha
I think it will rain tomorrow.
② Nepali grammar rules
1. लाग्छ and लाग्यो with a complete thought

**Experiencer + [content] + जस्तो लाग्छ** means “it seems to that person that …”.
The verb is the same लाग्नु as in **जाडो लाग्छ**, but here it takes the content of a thought.

rows:
मलाई उहाँ घरमा हुनुहुन्छ जस्तो लाग्छ।
malāī uhā̃ gharmā hunuhuncha jasto lāgcha
I think that person is at home. हुनुहुन्छ agrees with that person; लाग्छ belongs to the “seems to me” construction.

मलाई उहाँ घरमा हुनुहुन्छ जस्तो लाग्यो।
malāī uhā̃ gharmā hunuhuncha jasto lāgyo
I thought that person was at home. लाग्यो puts the impression in the past.

31.text: The order **मलाई लाग्छ, …** (malāī lāgcha, I think …) also occurs. **लाग्दैन** (lāgdaina) negates the impression.
2. हो, होला and हुन सक्छ (may be; can be)

**यो ठीक हो** (this is correct) asserts correctness; **यो ठीक होला** (this is probably correct) supposes it; **यो ठीक हुन सक्छ** (this may be correct) allows the possibility. होला and हुन सक्छ (may be; can be) do not encode fixed numerical probabilities.
3. Supposition about completion

**उहाँ जानुभएको होला** (he/she has probably gone) supposes that the person has gone.
 It combines respectful perfect **-नुभएको** with होला.
 Removing the modal and saying **जानुभयो** instead reports the event.
4. पर्छ: obligation versus inference
**Action in -नु + पर्छ expresses necessity. A perfect participle + हुनु पर्छ expresses an inference** about what must have happened. Read the preceding form.

rows:
उहाँलाई जानु पर्छ।
uhā̃lāī jānu parcha
That person needs to go: a required action.

उहाँ जानुभएको हुनु पर्छ।
uhā̃ jānubhaeko hunu parcha
That person must have gone: an inference from evidence.

31.text: **हुन सक्छ** (huna sakcha, may be) leaves a possibility open. Inferential **हुनु पर्छ** is also different from reporting a verified fact.
5. Scope of negation

**नआएको होला** (probably has not come) supposes non-arrival; **आउन सक्नुहुन्न** (cannot come, respectful) expresses inability to come; **आउनुभएको छैन** (has not come, respectful) states non-arrival.
 Preserve both the scope of negation and the presence/absence of supposition.

Practice focus: Respectful conjecture uses हुनुहोला, unlike a statement of fact with हुनुहुन्छ or a negative statement with हुनुहुन्न.
होला signals a conjecture (“probably”), unlike छ for stating a current condition as fact.
पर्छ has different roles in obligation and deduction.

32.text:
**Pattern and choice**
Passive खोलियो versus intransitive खुल्यो
**ढोका खोलियो** (the door was opened)

**ढोका खोलियो** (the door was opened) is passive was opened, from **खोल्नु**; **ढोका खुल्यो** (the door opened) is intransitive opened, from **खुल्नु**.
 Similar translated subjects do not make them the same verb construction.

Compare **लेखिन्छ/लेखियो/लेखिएन** for present, past and negative past passive.
 Active **लेख्छ** is not passive merely because its ending contains छ.

**शिक्षकद्वारा लेखिएको** (written by the teacher) names an agent in a formal passive modifier. **शिक्षकले लेख्नुभयो** (the teacher wrote it, respectful) is an active respectful clause.
 Changing perspective affects both participant marking and verb form.

**हुलाकमार्फत** means through the post; **प्रतिनिधिमार्फत** through a representative. मार्फत highlights a channel/intermediary, whereas द्वारा can identify an agent/means.
 Transmission through someone does not automatically make that person the agent.

**आज धेरै हिँडियो** (there was a lot of walking today) is an impersonal account of much walking, not a passive of a walked object. **म धेरै हिँडेँ** (I walked a lot) instead has an explicit first-person active subject.
Practice focus: The -इन्छ form expresses what is done, without foregrounding an agent. Distinguish it from first-person and respectful active forms.
Related forms taught in this topic

33.text:
**Pattern and choice**
Learn causative pairs
**खानु→खुवाउनु / सिक्नु→सिकाउनु / पढ्नु→पढाउनु**

Learn **खानु→खुवाउनु / सिक्नु→सिकाउनु / पढ्नु→पढाउनु**.
 These pairs include eat/feed and learn/teach.
 Causatives involve stem-specific changes, not one universally attachable ending.

In **आमाले बच्चालाई खाना खुवाउनुभयो** (the mother fed the child), आमाले is the causer, बच्चालाई the eater and खाना the food.
 Participant roles determine the marker selection.
3. लगाउनु and लाग्नु are different verbs
**Action in -न + लगाउनु (lagāunu) means to make/have someone do something**. It is a different verb from **लाग्नु (lāgnu), feel/take/seem**.

rows:
उहाँले मलाई लेख्न लगाउनुभयो।
uhā̃le malāī lekhna lagāunubhayo
That person had me write. उहाँले is the causer; मलाई is the writer; लेख्न is the action.

मलाई जाडो लाग्यो।
malāī jāḍo lāgyo
I felt/got cold. This लाग्यो is not causative.

33.text: The final **लगाउनुभयो** carries past tense and respect; the preceding लेख्न does not become लेख्नुभयो.
4. खुवाउनु versus खान दिनु (to let someone eat)

**खुवाउनु** expresses feeding/causing eating. **खान दिनु** (to let someone eat) can mean letting or allowing someone to eat.
 The translation feed/let eat depends on whether the action is caused or permitted.

Conjugate the causative itself: **सिकाउनुहुन्छ→सिकाउनुभयो→सिकाउनुभएन**.
 Compare ability **सिक्न सक्नुहुन्छ** (can learn, respectful) learn with **सिकाउन सक्नुहुन्छ** (can teach, respectful) teach; the causative stem remains essential.
Practice focus: Distinguish doing from causing: हाँस्नु → हँसाउनु, सुत्नु → सुताउनु, सिक्नु → सिकाउनु. Mark the affected person with लाई.

34.text:
**Pattern and choice**
Content + भन्नु
**उहाँले «म आउँछु» भन्नुभयो** (he/she said, “I will come”)
① Start with one example
**उहाँले जाँदिनँ भन्नुभयो।**
uhā̃le jā̃dinã bhannubhayo
She said she would not go.
② Nepali grammar rules
1. Content + भन्नु

In **उहाँले «म आउँछु» भन्नुभयो** (he/she said, “I will come”), quoted content precedes the reporting verb. **भन्नुभयो** is respectful past, **भन्नुहुन्छ** respectful present, agreeing with outer agent उहाँले.
2. From direct words to reported content
**म inside a quotation refers to the original speaker**. Compare preserving those words with reporting the content as “that they themselves …”.

rows:
उहाँले “म बिरामी छु” भन्नुभयो।
uhā̃le “ma birāmī chu” bhannubhayo
That person said, “I am ill.” The original छु stays inside the quotation.

उहाँले आफू बिरामी भएको बताउनुभयो।
uhā̃le āphū birāmī bhaeko batāunubhayo
That person reported being ill. आफू refers to that person; भएको connects the reported state.

34.text: **भएको is not a universal marker for every quotation.** An action can instead take a form such as **आफू आउने** (āphū āune, that they will come), according to the reported content.
3. भनेर, भन्ने and भने

**भनेर** links quoted content in **«आउँछु» भनेर भन्नुभयो** (said, “I will come”); **भन्ने** frames content in **आउने भन्ने कुरा** (the matter/content of coming). **भने** in **आउनुभयो भने** (if you/he/she comes, respectful) is conditional.
 Their shared shape does not give them one identical function.
4. Negation inside or outside the quote

**«आउँदिनँ» भन्नुभयो** (said, “I will not come”) reports saying I will not come. **«आउँछु» भन्नुभएन** (did not say, “I will come”) denies saying I will come.
 Moving negation across the quotation boundary changes what is asserted.
5. Time words and habitual reporting

Quoted **भोलि** is tomorrow relative to the original speech.
 Contrast habitual reporting **भन्नुहुन्थ्यो** with a completed report **भन्नुभयो**.
 Indirect reporting follows the intended time relations rather than obligatory English-style backshift.
Heard in conversation｜रे as a hearsay signal

Sentence-final **रे** can mark information heard from someone else.
 It does not assert that the speaker personally verified it.
 This reported-information use differs from the speaker’s own supposition with **होला**.
bholi chuṭṭī cha re.
I hear tomorrow is a day off.

Practice focus: these questions report a state with भएको, or a negative state with नभएको. आफू refers to the original speaker. Actions can take other forms; भएको is not a universal indirect-speech marker.
Direct quotation and indirect reporting

rows:
उहाँले “म बिरामी छु” भन्नुभयो।
uhā̃le “ma birāmī chu” bhannubhayo

उहाँले आफू बिरामी भएको बताउनुभयो।
uhā̃le āphū birāmī bhaeko batāunubhayo
She said that she was ill.

34.text: In direct speech, म refers to the original speaker.
Indirect reporting uses आफू, self, to refer back to the subject and बिरामी, ill, + भएको to package the reported state. बताउनुभयो is the respectful past of बताउनु, tell/report.

35.text:
**Pattern and choice**
लेख्नु present and negative
**लेख्नु→लेख्छु/लेख्दिनँ**

Compare **लेख्नु→लेख्छु/लेख्दिनँ**, we **लेख्छौं/लेख्दैनौं**, and respectful **लेख्नुहुन्छ/लेख्नुहुन्न**.
 The common stem participates in distinct ordinary/respectful present and negative patterns.

Compare **म चिठी लेख्छु** (I write a letter)→**मैले चिठी लेखेँ** (I wrote a letter).
 Transitive completion changes the subject marking too.
 Respectful past is **उहाँले चिठी लेख्नुभयो** (he/she wrote a letter, respectful); negative variants **लेखिनँ/लेखेनँ** differ from present लेख्दिनँ.

**लेख्दै छु** (I am writing) / **लेखेको छु** (I have written it) / **लेखेको थिएँ** (I had written it) express ongoing writing, present-relevant completion and prior completion at a past point.
 The auxiliary छु/थिएँ changes the reference time even with shared लेखेको.

**लेख्थें** is former habitual writing; **लेख्नेछु** future; **भोलि लेख्छु** (I will write tomorrow) a present-form plan.
 In **लेख्ने चिठी** (the letter to be written/that someone writes), लेख्ने modifies a noun rather than acting as a complete future predicate.

Compare **लेख्न सक्छु** (I can write) / **लेख्न चाहन्छु** (I want to write) / **लेख्नु पर्छ** (need to write) / **लेख्नको लागि** (in order to write).
 Ability/desire use लेख्न, basic necessity लेख्नु, and purpose लेख्नको लागि (in order to write).
 The complement construction determines the preceding form.

Practice focus: Present, I: लेख्नु → लेख्छु.
Negative present, we: लेख्नु → लेख्दैनौं.
Future, we: लेख्नु → लेख्नेछौं.
Past, respectful: लेख्नु → लेख्नुभयो. Mark the agent with ले.
See topic 7 for respect/familiarity and topics 1–2 for **हो**/छ.
This appendix uses लेख्नु, to write.
Starting from the stem लेख्, compare who writes, who wrote and who has written.

That person does not write letters.

You all wrote a letter yesterday.

36.text:
**Pattern and choice**
Three sets with one subject
**म लेखक हुँ** (I am an author) / **म घरमा छु** (I am at home) / **म बिहान घरमा हुन्छु** (I am usually at home in the morning)
① Start with one example
ma lekhak hũ
I am an author.
② Nepali grammar rules
1. Three sets with one subject

Compare **म लेखक हुँ** (I am an author) / **म घरमा छु** (I am at home) / **म बिहान घरमा हुन्छु** (I am usually at home in the morning): identity, current location and habitual setting.
 All belong to हुनु, but the construction and intended perspective select the set.
2. Three negative sets

Compare **हुँ→होइनँ / छु→छैनँ / हुन्छु→हुँदिनँ**, and ordinary **होइन/छैन/हुँदैन**.
 Respectful **हुनुहुन्न** can serve multiple functions; interpret the surrounding identity/location/habitual construction.
3. Past state versus occurrence

**म घरमा थिएँ** (I was at home) describes a past location; **काम भयो** (the work was done/accomplished) accomplishment/occurrence.
 Distinguish **थियो** from **भयो**.
 Respectful past states use **हुनुहुन्थ्यो**; respectful occurrences include **हुनुभयो**.
4. Shared honorific forms, distinct functions

**उहाँ लेखक हुनुहुन्छ** (he/she is an author, respectful) / **उहाँ घरमा हुनुहुन्छ** (he/she is at home, respectful) share an honorific verb, but differ in identity noun versus मा-marked location. **उहाँलाई जाडो लाग्छ** (he/she feels cold, respectful) is a dative-experiencer construction with लाग्नु, not an interchangeable हुनु clause.
5. छ and थियो as auxiliaries

In **पढ्दै छु** (I am reading) / **पढेको छु** (I have read it) / **पढेको थिएँ** (I had read it), छु/थिएँ act as auxiliaries for progression/completion.
 Their preceding verb forms distinguish these from location **घरमा छु** (I am at home).
 See topics 10, 15 and 16.
हुनु: three sets and matching forms

rows: Topic 4; also permission in 21 and prohibition in 19

म विद्यार्थी हुँ।
ma vidyārthī hũ
Identity, so the हो set: topic 1

म घरमा छु।
ma gharmā chu
Location, so the छ set: topic 2

म बिहान घरमा हुन्छु।
ma bihān gharmā hunchu
I am usually at home in the morning.
A regular time setting, so the हुन्छ set: topic 4

36.text: हो set: six basic person groups, positive and negative

हुन्छ set: six basic person groups, positive and negative

Practice focus: Identity uses the हो family: हामी takes हौं. Distinguish location छौं and habitual/change हुन्छौं.
A current state uses the छ family: म takes छु, unlike identity हुँ or habitual/change हुन्छु.
A regular location can use the हुन्छ family: म takes हुन्छु. Contrast this habitual context with छु for a location right now.
See topic 7 for respect/familiarity and topics 1–2 for **हो**/छ.
Choose a form of हुनु according to what you mean.

learningPath.title: Your first 7 steps
learningPath.description: Five sentences at a time: read the pattern, say your answer, then check the text and audio. This is a suggested order; you can start anywhere.

intro.title: Start with sound and reading
intro.body: Use the romanization alongside the recording. म विद्यार्थी हुँ (ma vidyārthī hũ) means “I am a student.” Reveal the answer in practice, listen and say it aloud.

intro.title: Notice a and ā
intro.body: a and ā represent different vowel qualities; ā is the more open vowel. The bars in ī and ū also preserve spelling distinctions. Do not assume every bar means exactly twice the length: follow the recording.

intro.title: Listen for the extra breath
intro.body: Pairs such as k/kh and t/th differ in aspiration. With kh, release an extra puff of air after k. th is not English “th.” A dot in ṭ or ḍ marks a tongue position farther back than t or d.

intro.title: Some vowels have a nasal quality
intro.body: The tilde in यहाँ (yahā̃, “here”) marks a nasal vowel. Let the vowel resonate through the nose; do not simply add a separate n. Listen for this in हुँ (hũ, “I am”) too.

intro.title: Build from the ending
intro.body: म विद्यार्थी हुँ follows “I + student + am.” Verbs usually come at the end, but their forms change with person and respect. Begin with म (I), हामी (we), तपाईं (you) and उहाँ (he/she, respectful), then learn the roles of हो, छ and हुन्छ.

steps.title: Introduce yourself and others
steps.goal: Use the हो family for identity and choose an ending for the person.

steps.title: Say where someone or something is
steps.goal: Use the छ family for location and existence, including negative sentences.

steps.title: Describe states and qualities
steps.goal: Use the छ family with qualities such as busy or cold.

steps.title: Talk about regular situations
steps.goal: Use हुन्छ for regular or general situations.

steps.title: Connect places and people
steps.goal: Compare मा, बाट and सँग in complete sentences.

steps.title: Ask a useful question
steps.goal: Ask about things, ownership, places, amounts and people.

steps.title: Say your introduction aloud
steps.goal: Try short conversation sentences about your name, background and home.

levels.desc1: Basic words and short sentences. Practical everyday expressions.
levels.desc2: Complex sentences and conjunctions. Conversation and explanation.
levels.desc3: Abstract content and idioms. Complex grammatical structures.

learningPathV2.title: Your first 7 steps
learningPathV2.description: Three new sentences per step. Meet the words, choose a form, choose a meaning, then build the model. Sentences without a conjugation task start with meaning. Explore in any order and use hints freely.

intro.title: Text, reading and meaning together
intro.body: Start by listening to one sentence. Use its reading and translation to follow unfamiliar letters.

intro.title: Listen to अ and आ
intro.body: a and ā mark different vowels in this reading system. Listen to the vowel quality; do not assume ā must always be twice as long.

intro.title: क and ख: the puff of air
intro.body: ख (kha) has a stronger puff of air than क (ka). Listen to it as one consonant, not a separate k followed by h.

intro.title: त and ट: tongue position
intro.body: For त (ta), the tongue tip touches the upper teeth. For ट (ṭa), it is farther back. The dot in ṭ distinguishes the sounds.

intro.title: A tilde marks a nasal vowel
intro.body: The ā̃ in यहाँ and ũ in हुँ are nasal vowels. Let the vowel resonate through the nose; do not add a separate n.

intro.title: The subject changes the ending
intro.body: म (I) takes हुँ; respectful तपाईं (you) takes हुनुहुन्छ. Listen to the two complete sentences.

steps.title: Introduce yourself and others
steps.goal: Use the हो family for identity and choose an ending for the person.

steps.title: Say where someone or something is
steps.goal: Use the छ family for location and existence, including negative sentences.

steps.title: Describe states and qualities
steps.goal: Use the छ family with qualities such as busy or cold.

steps.title: Talk about regular situations
steps.goal: Use हुन्छ for regular or general situations.

steps.title: Connect places and people
steps.goal: Compare मा, बाट and सँग in complete sentences.

steps.title: Ask a useful question
steps.goal: Ask about things, ownership, places, amounts and people.

steps.title: Say your introduction aloud
steps.goal: Try short conversation sentences about your name, background and home.

steps.title: Theme 1｜हो: A is B (identity / equation)
steps.goal: For identity: म → हुँ, हामी → हौं, तपाईं/उहाँ → हुनुहुन्छ.

steps.title: Theme 2｜छ: existence and location
steps.goal: For location now: म → छु, हामी → छौं; respectful तपाईं/उहाँ → हुनुहुन्छ.

steps.title: Theme 3｜छ: is ~ (adjective / state)
steps.goal: An adjective + the छ family describes a current state: I → छु, we → छौं, respectful subjects → हुनुहुन्छ.

steps.title: Theme 4｜हुन्छ: becomes / generally is (habitual, change)
steps.goal: Use हुन्छ for recurring or general conditions; its negative is हुँदैन. Distinguish these from a state just now.

steps.title: Theme 5｜Postpositions: place, participants and relationships
steps.goal:
बाट marks a source of movement, सम्म an endpoint, and मा a location. Attach each after the noun.
Use सँग for an accompanying person, unlike endpoint सम्म or source बाट.

steps.title: Theme 6｜Question words and how to ask
steps.goal: Choose कहिले for time, कहाँ for place, and किन for a reason.

steps.title: Theme 7｜Pronouns, familiarity, respect and verb agreement
steps.goal: Match respect level: ऊ → छ, उनी → छन्, तिमी → छौ, उहाँ → हुनुहुन्छ. Here उनी refers to one person.

steps.title: Theme 8｜Action verbs: present (do ~)
steps.goal: Present actions and routines agree with the subject: म → -छु, हामी → -छौं, respectful subjects → -नुहुन्छ.

steps.title: Theme 9｜Present negative (don't ~)
steps.goal: Match a present negative to its subject: the -दिनँ family with म, -दैनौं with हामी, and -नुहुन्न for respect. Vowel-stem verbs also change within the stem.

steps.title: Theme 10｜Present progressive (~ing)
steps.goal: An ongoing action uses -दै/-तै plus the छ family, with the auxiliary agreeing with the subject.

steps.title: Theme 11｜The ergative ले & the past (did ~)
steps.goal: Completed transitive actions mark the agent with ले: म → मैले, हामी → हामीले, तपाईं → तपाईंले, उहाँ → उहाँले.

steps.title: Theme 12｜Past negative (didn't ~)
steps.goal: Compare past negatives: the first-person -इनँ family, plural -एनौं, and respectful -नुभएन.

steps.title: Theme 13｜Future (will ~)
steps.goal: Future forms agree with the subject: -नेछु for I, -नेछौं for we, -नुहुनेछ for respectful subjects.

steps.title: Theme 14｜Habitual past (used to ~)
steps.goal: Use the past habitual for former routines: बस्नु becomes बस्थें with म, बस्थ्यौं with हामी, and बस्नुहुन्थ्यो for respect.

steps.title: Theme 15｜Present perfect / experience (have done ~)
steps.goal: Perfect/experience uses the -एको family + छ: masculine -एको, feminine -एकी, plural -एका, respectful -नुभएको.

steps.title: Theme 16｜Past perfect (had done ~)
steps.goal: For completion before a past reference time, use a perfect form + the थियो family: I → थिएँ, we → थियौं, respectful -नुभएको → थियो.

उहाँले हिजो बेलुकासम्म पत्र लेख्नुभएको थियो।
मैले हिजो बेलुकासम्म पत्र लेखेको थिएँ।
हामीले हिजो बेलुकासम्म दूध पिएका थियौं।
उहाँले हिजो बेलुकासम्म दूध पिउनुभएको थियो।
मैले हिजो बेलुकासम्म पत्र लेखेकी थिएँ।
हामीले हिजो बेलुकासम्म स्याउ खाएका थियौं।

उहाँले हिजो बेलुकासम्म नेपाली सिक्नुभएको थियो।

steps.title: Theme 17｜Requests & commands (three politeness levels)
steps.goal: A polite request uses -नुहोस्. Distinguish it from descriptive -नुहुन्छ and first-person -छु.

steps.title: Theme 18｜Hortative / volitional (let's ~ / shall I ~)
steps.goal: Use -औं for “let us”. Distinguish it from habitual “we” forms in -छौं and requests in -नुहोस्.

steps.title: Theme 19｜Prohibition (must not ~ / don't ~)
steps.goal: A polite prohibition adds न before the request form: न…नुहोस्. Adding न reverses the meaning.

steps.title: Theme 20｜Ability (can ~)
steps.goal: Ability uses a verb’s -न form + सक्नु. Match the auxiliary: सक्छु, सक्छौं, or respectful सक्नुहुन्छ.

steps.title: Theme 21｜Obligation & permission (must ~ / may ~)
steps.goal: After -न, पाइन्छ means allowed, पाइँदैन means not allowed, and पर्छ means must. These differ from ability with सक्नु.

steps.title: Theme 22｜Desire (want to ~)
steps.goal: For a wish, use the experiencer + लाई, a verb in -न, and मन छ. मन छ stays the same when the person changes.

steps.title: Theme 23｜Adjective agreement & position
steps.goal:
Match an inflecting adjective to the noun: masculine singular सानो, feminine singular सानी, plural साना.
यी and the noun ending -हरू indicate plural. Match the adjective साना and possessive मेरा.
केटी (girl) is feminine singular, so use सानी rather than सानो.

items.ne: यो सानी केटी आज खुसी छ।
यो सानी केटी अहिले खुसी छ।
यो सानी केटी यहाँ खुसी छ।
यो सानी केटी त्यहाँ खुसी छ।
यो सानी केटी बिहान खुसी छ।
यो सानी केटी बेलुका खुसी छ।

steps.title: Theme 24｜Adverbs & exclamations
steps.goal: Adverbs describe manner or repetition: बिस्तारै slowly, छिटो quickly, फेरि again. They do not agree with the subject.

steps.title: Theme 25｜Comparison & superlative
steps.goal:
Attach भन्दा to the comparison standard for “than”. The adjective itself does not need a comparative ending.
सबैभन्दा literally compares with all: “the most”. Distinguish it from अलि (a little) and धेरै (very).
For equal degree use जत्तिकै: त्योजत्तिकै means “as … as that”, unlike भन्दा for a difference.

steps.title: Theme 26｜Conjunctions (and / so / but)
steps.goal:
तर connects a contrast (“but”), unlike additive र (“and”) or reason-giving किनभने (“because”).
र can connect actions and clauses as “and”, as well as connecting nouns.
Use त्यसैले for reason → result (“so”), and किनभने when a reason follows a result (“because”).

items.ne: यो किताब महँगो छ तर राम्रो छ।
म बिरामी छु त्यसैले म घरमा बस्छु।
म घरमा बस्छु किनभने म बिरामी छु।
यो झोला महँगो छ तर राम्रो छ।
म थकित छु त्यसैले म घरमा बस्छु।
म घरमा बस्छु किनभने म थकित छु।
यो कोठा महँगो छ तर राम्रो छ।
म व्यस्त छु त्यसैले म घरमा बस्छु।
म घरमा बस्छु किनभने म व्यस्त छु।
यो नक्सा महँगो छ तर राम्रो छ।
यो छाता महँगो छ तर राम्रो छ।
यो कलम महँगो छ तर राम्रो छ।
यो टिकट महँगो छ तर राम्रो छ।

steps.title: Theme 27｜While ~ (-दै) / after ~ (-एपछि)
steps.goal: -एपछि means after completing an action; -दै/-तै expresses simultaneous “while”. Choose by the timing of the actions.

steps.title: Theme 28｜In order to ~ (-नको लागि)
steps.goal: The verb ending -नको लागि expresses purpose (“in order to”), distinct from पछि (after) and अघि (before).

steps.title: Theme 29｜Relative expressions: people, things, place and time
steps.goal:
Relative जो refers to a person and pairs here with उसले. Distinguish place कहाँ/जहाँ and time कहिले/जब.
जब … तब … pairs “when … then …”. It refers to time, not a person or place.
जहाँ … त्यहीँ … refers to a place and points back to it. Distinguish interrogative कहाँ from relative जहाँ.

items.ne: जब उहाँ नेपाली पढ्नुहुन्छ तब हामी सिक्छौं।
जहाँ विद्यालय छ हामी त्यहीँ जान्छौं।
जब उहाँ पत्र लेख्नुहुन्छ तब हामी सिक्छौं।
जहाँ पुस्तकालय छ हामी त्यहीँ जान्छौं।
जब उहाँ गीत गाउनुहुन्छ तब हामी सिक्छौं।
जहाँ पसल छ हामी त्यहीँ जान्छौं।
जब उहाँ खाना पकाउनुहुन्छ तब हामी सिक्छौं।
जहाँ बजार छ हामी त्यहीँ जान्छौं।
जब उहाँ साइकल चलाउनुहुन्छ तब हामी सिक्छौं।
जहाँ कार्यालय छ हामी त्यहीँ जान्छौं।
जब उहाँ फोटो खिच्नुहुन्छ तब हामी सिक्छौं।
जहाँ पार्क छ हामी त्यहीँ जान्छौं।
जब उहाँ अंग्रेजी बोल्नुहुन्छ तब हामी सिक्छौं।

steps.title: Theme 30｜Conditionals (if ~)
steps.goal: भए introduces a condition (“if there is”). भएपछि means after that happens; भएर links a cause/circumstance.

items.ne: आज समय भए म नेपाली पढ्नेछु।
भोलि समय भए म नेपाली पढ्नेछु।
आज फुर्सद भए म नेपाली पढ्नेछु।
भोलि फुर्सद भए म नेपाली पढ्नेछु।
आज समय भए म पत्र लेख्नेछु।
भोलि समय भए म पत्र लेख्नेछु।
आज फुर्सद भए म पत्र लेख्नेछु।
भोलि फुर्सद भए म पत्र लेख्नेछु।
आज समय भए म गीत गाउनेछु।
भोलि समय भए म गीत गाउनेछु।
आज फुर्सद भए म गीत गाउनेछु।
भोलि फुर्सद भए म गीत गाउनेछु।
आज समय भए म खाना पकाउनेछु।
भोलि समय भए म खाना पकाउनेछु।
आज फुर्सद भए म खाना पकाउनेछु।
भोलि फुर्सद भए म खाना पकाउनेछु।
आज समय भए म साइकल चलाउनेछु।
भोलि समय भए म साइकल चलाउनेछु।
आज फुर्सद भए म साइकल चलाउनेछु।
भोलि फुर्सद भए म साइकल चलाउनेछु।

steps.title: Theme 31｜Inference / opinion / possibility (I think / probably / might / must be)
steps.goal:
Respectful conjecture uses हुनुहोला, unlike a statement of fact with हुनुहुन्छ or a negative statement with हुनुहुन्न.
होला signals a conjecture (“probably”), unlike छ for stating a current condition as fact.

steps.title: Theme 32｜Passive (be ~ed)
steps.goal: The -इन्छ form expresses what is done, without foregrounding an agent. Distinguish it from first-person and respectful active forms.

steps.title: Theme 33｜Causative (make someone ~)
steps.goal: Distinguish doing from causing: हाँस्नु → हँसाउनु, सुत्नु → सुताउनु, सिक्नु → सिकाउनु. Mark the affected person with लाई.

steps.title: Theme 34｜Reported speech (said that ~)
steps.goal: In this report, भएको links the content “being”; नभएको links “not being”. आफू refers to the reported speaker.

steps.title: Theme 35 (Appendix A)｜Verb forms through writing: लेख्नु
steps.goal:
Present, I: लेख्नु → लेख्छु.
Negative present, we: लेख्नु → लेख्दैनौं.
Future, we: लेख्नु → लेख्नेछौं.
Past, respectful: लेख्नु → लेख्नुभयो. Mark the agent with ले.

steps.title: Theme 36 (Appendix B)｜Copulas through identity and location
steps.goal:
Identity uses the हो family: हामी takes हौं. Distinguish location छौं and habitual/change हुन्छौं.
A current state uses the छ family: म takes छु, unlike identity हुँ or habitual/change हुन्छु.
A regular location can use the हुन्छ family: म takes हुन्छु. Contrast this habitual context with छु for a location right now.

sections.title: How the script works
sections.body:
Nepali is read left to right. A consonant letter includes an inherent a: क is ka and स is sa. The consonant chart in this course uses these letter readings.
The lower mark ् (halant) removes that a: क् is k and स् is s, without a following vowel. Compare the two pairs below.
When consonants join, as in स् + त = स्त (sta), there is no vowel between s and t.

samples.detail: Unlike क, this has no final a. Do not add another vowel after k.
Only the airflow sound: do not add a vowel after s.

sections.title: 11 vowel letters
sections.body:
These are independent vowel letters. The i and u sounds each have two spellings. Roman bars also help distinguish those spellings.
An independent letter is also used when a vowel follows another vowel.

samples.detail: This is the inherent vowel in a plain consonant letter.
Compare its quality with अ. The bar does not mean you must simply double its duration.
The sign ि appears to the left but is pronounced after the consonant: कि = ki.
Keep इ and ई distinct in spelling. Modern Nepali does not consistently distinguish them by duration alone.
After a consonant, use the lower sign ु: कु = ku.
Distinguish उ and ऊ in writing. Notice the shape of ू; do not memorise a fixed two-to-one duration rule.

samples.meaning: A letter mainly in Sanskrit-derived words
samples.detail: Usually read close to ri in Nepali. Its dependent sign is ृ. Learn it after the common vowel letters.
Listen with a steady mouth shape. Its dependent sign is े.
Its dependent sign is ै. Compare the marks above the letter with ए’s े.
Its dependent sign ो has parts around the consonant but represents one vowel.
Its sign ौ differs from ओ’s ो at the top.

sections.title: 33 consonants without a vowel
sections.body:
Adding ् removes a consonant letter’s inherent a: क → क् (k), स → स् (s). The roman spelling also has no final a.
Here are the vowel-free forms of all 33 core consonants. क् and स् have play icons as representative recordings; the other 31 entries are a written reference.
When consonants join, they can form half-letters or ligatures. Explore their joined shapes in Conjuncts.

sections.title: At the back: the क group
sections.body:
Raise the back of the tongue. Compare the puff of air in क/ख and ग/घ. ङ is a nasal sound at the same place; it also appears in clusters such as ङ्ग.
These recordings read consonant letters with inherent a. A vowel-free consonant is written with ्, as in क्.

sections.title: The च and ज group
sections.body:
Compare the aspiration in च/छ and ज/झ. Roman c here marks a ch/ts-like sound, not k. ञ is mainly encountered in conjuncts.
These recordings read consonant letters with inherent a. A vowel-free consonant is written with ्, as in क्.

sections.title: Tongue farther back: ट group
sections.body:
Place the tongue tip farther back than the upper teeth. The dots in ṭ and ḍ distinguish these from त and द. Compare with the next group.
These recordings read consonant letters with inherent a. A vowel-free consonant is written with ्, as in क्.

samples.meaning: Retroflex nasal; often close to न in everyday speech

sections.title: At the upper teeth: त group
sections.body:
Touch the tongue tip near the upper teeth. त and ट are distinct letters and sounds. The h in थ marks aspiration, not an extra syllable.
These recordings read consonant letters with inherent a. A vowel-free consonant is written with ्, as in क्.

sections.title: Using the lips: प group
sections.body:
Close and release the lips. Compare aspiration in प/फ and ब/भ. फ can also be pronounced close to f, especially in loanwords.
These recordings read consonant letters with inherent a. A vowel-free consonant is written with ्, as in क्.

sections.title: Eight more consonants
sections.body:
य, र, ल, व and श, ष, स, ह. श and ष occur in Sanskrit-derived spellings and may approach स in everyday speech. Learn both the spelling and the spoken form.
These recordings read consonant letters with inherent a. A vowel-free consonant is written with ्, as in क्.

samples.meaning: V/w-like; varies by word and speaker
The letter ष; often close to s

sections.title: Consonant + vowel
sections.body:
Explore 33 consonants × 11 vowels. For example, म + ा = मा and म + ि = मि: the consonant stays, the vowel changes.
Start with क, म and न. The ऋ/ृ column and some combinations are spelling references; not every combination is common in everyday words.
Notice the special shapes रु and रू.

sections.title: Conjunct consonants
sections.body:
The lower mark ् (halant) removes the inherent vowel. In क् + त = क्त, the consonants join without a vowel between. Shapes may become half-forms, stack, or change considerably.
क्ष, त्र, ज्ञ and श्र are combinations too. ज्ञ is commonly read close to gya in Nepali; क्ष varies toward kṣ/chya by word and speaker.
Initial र् may appear above (र्क); following र often attaches below (क्र, त्र).
These 30 common forms illustrate the patterns. Conjuncts are productive combinations, not a finite extra alphabet. Listen to each whole word.

sections.title: Nasal sounds and signs
sections.body:
ँ (chandrabindu) marks a nasal vowel: let the vowel resonate through the nose rather than adding a separate n. ं (anusvara) marks nasal sound; its pronunciation can adapt to the following consonant.
ः (visarga) occurs mainly in Sanskrit-derived spelling; check the whole word’s pronunciation. । marks a sentence ending.

sections.title: Digits and reading
sections.body:
Digits also run left to right: १० is 10 and २५ is 25. Number names are not made simply by reading each digit separately; begin with 0–9.
This course covers the core Nepali script. The wider script also has letters such as ॠ, ऌ and ॡ for classical or other-language use, and dotted letters (़) for borrowed sounds. Those are distinct from the 33 core consonants and 11 vowel letters.

note.ja: 時間の長さを数えます。「3時」のような時刻には बजे を使います。
note.en: Counts hours of duration. Use बजे for clock times such as three o’clock.

senses.ja: たくさんの・たくさん・とても

note.ja: 肯定なら「まったく・完全に」。否定と組み合わせると「全然〜ない」です。
note.en: Means completely or absolutely; with a negative, not at all.

senses.ja: めったに〜ない・まれに

note.ja: 「確信」という名詞のほか、「確かに」という副詞にもなります。निश्चय नै もよく使う形です。
note.en: Used as a noun for certainty and an adverb for certainly. निश्चय नै is also common.

senses.ja: 誤った・間違っている
本当のことを話す・正直な
身軽な・きびきびした

examples.ja: 私はネパールに住んでいます。

senses.ja: つかむ・捕まえる・握る
置く・しまう・保管する

examples.ja: ここにごみを捨てないでください。
examples.en: Please do not throw rubbish here.

note.ja: 物を「投げる」だけでなく、不要な物を「捨てる」にも使います。फोहोर फाल्नु＝ごみを捨てる。
note.en: Used both for throwing and discarding. फोहोर फाल्नु means throw away rubbish.

examples.ja: 私たちはご飯を食べます。

senses.ja: 塗る・付ける・取り付ける
〜できる（動詞の -न 形と使う）
senses.en: can; be able to (after a verb in -न)

examples.ja: 私はネパール語を読めます。

note.ja: 動詞の -न 形＋सक्नु は「〜できる」。काम सक्नु のように目的語を伴うと「仕事を終える」の意味にもなります。
note.en: Verb in -न + सक्नु expresses ability. With an object, as in काम सक्नु, it can mean finish the work.

note.ja: मलाई जाडो लाग्छ＝私は寒く感じます。時間の長さ＋लाग्छ なら「〜かかる」。मलाई … लाग्छ には「〜と思う・感じる」の用法もあります。
note.en: मलाई जाडो लाग्छ means I feel cold. A duration + लाग्छ means it takes that long. मलाई … लाग्छ also expresses impressions or opinions.

senses.ja: 知るようになる・分かる

note.ja: 情報を得て「分かる・知るようになる」。すでに知っている状態は थाहा हुनु：मलाई थाहा छ。
note.en: Finding out is a change. For already knowing, use थाहा हुनु: मलाई थाहा छ।

note.ja: 「主語＋好きなもの＋मन पराउनु」。मलाई … मन पर्छ の形も使います。
note.en: Used with a subject and something they like. मलाई … मन पर्छ is another common pattern.

note.ja: 兄弟の息子です。姉妹の息子は भान्जा。いとことは区別します。
note.en: A brother’s son. A sister’s son is भान्जा; this is not a cousin.

note.ja: 兄弟の娘です。姉妹の娘は भान्जी。
note.en: A brother’s daughter. A sister’s daughter is भान्जी.

senses.ja: 新生児・生まれたばかりの
うんざりした・退屈した
よい・大丈夫な・正しい
気に入っている・好きな
気に入らない・好きでない
影響を受けた・感銘を受けた

note.ja: 基本は茶色。灰色は खरानी रङ्ग などで表します。
note.en: Normally brown. Grey can be expressed as खरानी रङ्ग.

senses.ja: 半ズボン・パンツ（下着）
ダウラスルワル(民族衣装)
鎖・チェーン／衣服のファスナー
野菜のおかず・カレー
おいしい食べ物・料理

note.ja: 水を表しますが、पानी पर्छ のような天気の文では雨の意味になります。
note.en: Means water; in weather expressions such as पानी पर्छ it refers to rain.

senses.ja: ミルクを入れない紅茶

note.ja: 月を表す名詞と、英語由来の6月は同じ綴りです。関係表現の जुन（〜するところの）もあります。
note.en: The moon and the borrowed month name June share this spelling. जुन also has a relative use: which/that.

senses.ja: 幹線道路・ハイウェイ

note.en: The activity of sewing, not the person. A tailor is दर्जी.

senses.en: cutting hair; a person who cuts hair

note.ja: 学校の「学期・期間」という名詞のほか、数詞の「17」と同じ綴りになります。
note.en: The noun for an academic session shares its spelling with the number seventeen.

note.ja: 「返す・戻す」こと。お釣りだけに限定しません。
note.en: Returning something or a refund; not limited to change from a purchase.

senses.ja: 遊び・ゲーム・スポーツ

note.ja: 「庭仕事をする」という表現。名詞の「園芸」は बागवानी。
note.en: A phrase for working in a garden. The noun gardening is बागवानी.

senses.ja: 雪を頂く高山・ヒマラヤ山脈

note.ja: 名詞「援助」です。「助けてください」は सहयोग गर्नुहोस् など、依頼の文にします。
note.en: A noun meaning assistance. Make a request, for example सहयोग गर्नुहोस्, to ask for help.

senses.ja: 石こう・ギプス／ばんそうこう

senses.en: break a bone; a bone breaks

senses.ja: 〜である・いる・ある／〜になる

note.ja: हो 系は身元・種類、छ 系は存在・状態、हुन्छ 系は習慣・一般的な成り立ちなど。主語の人称と敬意によって形が変わります。
note.en: हो forms identify; छ forms describe existence/state; हुन्छ forms express habitual/general situations. Forms also depend on person and respect.

senses.ja: 落ちる・降る／必要になる・費用がかかる

note.ja: पानी पर्छ＝雨が降る。जानुपर्छ＝行かなければならない。कति पर्छ?＝いくらかかりますか。文型ごとに意味を確認します。
note.en: पानी पर्छ: it rains. जानुपर्छ: must go. कति पर्छ?: how much does it cost? The construction determines the meaning.

senses.ja: 合う・一致する／可能である・許される
senses.en: match; fit; be possible; be permitted

note.ja: 口語の यहाँ बस्न मिल्छ? は「ここに座ってもいいですか」。-न मिल्छ で可能・許可をたずねる形です。
note.en: The colloquial question यहाँ बस्न मिल्छ? means May I sit here? A verb in -न + मिल्छ can express possibility or permission.

senses.ja: あの方・彼・彼女（敬意）
あの方々・彼ら・彼女ら（敬意）
彼・彼女（中程度の敬意）
君・あなた（親しい間柄）

examples.ja: 私は日本から来ました。
私は朝からここにいます。
examples.en: I have been here since morning.

senses.ja: 動作主・手段を示す助詞

examples.ja: 水がないと植物は枯れます。

note.ja: 「死ぬ」の基本形です。「殺す」は मार्नु。人の死を丁寧に伝えるときは निधन हुनु などを使います。
note.en: The basic verb for die. मार्नु means kill. निधन हुनु is a respectful expression for a person passing away.

examples.ja: 魚は水の中で生きています。
私は日本で生まれました。

note.ja: 「殺す」という他動詞です。मर्नु（死ぬ）と、ा の有無が違います。
note.en: A transitive verb meaning kill. Distinguish मार्नु from मर्नु, die: the vowel sign ा changes the word.

examples.ja: ここで車を止めてください。

note.ja: 人が物や動きを「止める」。物や動きが「止まる」は रोकिनु。
note.en: Stopping something. रोकिनु means coming to a stop.

senses.ja: 目を覚ます・起きている

note.ja: お風呂やシャワーで体を洗うこと。服や食器などを洗う動詞とは使い分けます。
note.en: Bathing or washing oneself, including showering. Other verbs are used for washing clothes or dishes.

senses.ja: 磨く・こすり洗いする
離す・置いていく・やめる

examples.ja: 私はかばんを家に置いてきました。

note.en: Recognizing a person or being acquainted with them. Use थाहा हुनु for knowing information.

note.ja: 望む人を主語にします。म जान चाहन्छु＝私は行きたいです。必要を表す चाहिनु と区別します。
note.en: The person wanting is the subject. म जान चाहन्छु means I want to go. Distinguish चाहिनु, be needed.

note.ja: 必要な物が主語になります。मलाई पानी चाहिन्छ＝私には水が必要です。
note.en: The needed thing is the subject. मलाई पानी चाहिन्छ means I need water.
